structure: Part 17, the panel rulings ledger. Read in full: spec/panel/README.md (35 lines), spec/panel/rulings.json (3008 lines) and spec/panel/critic.json (183 lines) under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants. The slice stops at decisions.json and conflicts.json, which part 16 claims. README.md says what the panel is (rulings on the spec's conflicts and open questions), that ../decisions.json is the ledger and the only place a ruling lives, that these two files are the evidence behind it, what the standing rulings for the 2026-09-06 first pass are, and the three-step procedure for changing a ruling. rulings.json holds decidedAt 2026-09-06, eight dockets with a summary and ruling count each (D1 territory and timing 11, D4 parties and contact 5, D2 commodity model 15, D8 scope and parked 17, D3 origin values and validation 11, D5 reference, status and lifecycle 7, D6 chrome and journey shape 7, D7 non-functional 10 — 83 in all), the 83 rulings in docket order with docket, id, kind (conflict or behaviour), ruling (resolve, adopt or park), resolution, rationale, specChanges, dissent, escalate and decidedBy (panel or sam), and a 55-entry reconciliation array recording every edit the consistency critic's findings caused, with before, after and why per entry plus three docket-summary rewrites. critic.json holds an empty missingIds list, 14 cross-docket inconsistencies each with its issue and proposed fix, five standing-ruling-breach entries, and a summary. Covered: all 8 docket ids and summaries; all 83 rulings, one claim each with the docket, what it decides, who decided it and the reasoning, plus extra claims for the copy strings and corrections the rulings fix; the reconciliation block by chair decision (1 to 12) and the global target normalisation; every critic entry and the answer given; and three gaps (the unstated wording of standing rulings 1, 4 and 5; no judge or chair is named; no ruling carries a decisions.json ledger id).

claims.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps a judges panel whose rulings settle the spec's conflicts and open questions, with one ledger entry per ruling stamped onto its subject.
claims.quote:
# Judges panel — rulings on the spec's conflicts and open questions

`../decisions.json` is the ledger: one entry per ruling, stamped onto its
subject (a conflict's `resolution` and `decision`, or a behaviour's `status`
and `decision`).

claims.statement: decisions.json is the only place a ruling lives; conflicts.json and the behaviours carry a pointer to it and never their own answer.
claims.quote: It is the only place a ruling lives; conflicts.json and the behaviours carry a pointer to it, never their own answer.

claims.statement: rulings.json and critic.json are kept as the evidence behind the ledger so a ruling can be revisited with its reasoning: rulings.json holds eight dockets with three judges and a chair each and one ruling per item with rationale, spec changes, dissent and who decided it (panel, or sam where a standing product-owner ruling settled it), and a reconciliation array recording every edit the critic's findings caused; critic.json holds the critic's report of coverage, cross-docket contradictions and breaches of the standing rulings.

claims.statement: Six subjects are standing rulings out of phase for the first pass dated 2026-09-06 — users, sign-in models, agents, delegation of authority, plant-operator registration and 'who notifies' — and bulk upload is also out of phase; both are parked, not rejected.

claims.statement: Changing a ruling leaves rulings.json and critic.json alone and edits the ledger and its subject in one commit: a new d-NNN entry with status current, supersedes and decidedAt; the earlier entry set superseded with supersededBy; and the subject re-stamped (a conflict's resolution, resolvedBy and decision, or a behaviour's status and decision plus ' | Ruling: <resolution>' appended to its detail).
claims.quote:
To change a ruling, leave the two files here alone and edit the ledger and
its subject in one commit:

1. Append an entry to `../decisions.json` with the next `d-NNN` id,
   `status: "current"`, `supersedes` set to the earlier entry's id and
   `decidedAt` set to the date of the ruling.
2. Set the earlier entry's `status` to `"superseded"` and its
   `supersededBy` to the new id.
3. Re-stamp the subject.

claims.statement: Docket D1-territory-and-timing (11 rulings) settles territory and timing: every notifier-facing string says Great Britain with no nation check on any address, plants and wood answer a Yes/No arrival-status question before giving one date and a destination while potatoes give an expected date and time and are never asked whether they have arrived, the arrival date is validated only as a real calendar date with one sourced bound, and lateness is computed in calendar days by one pure helper, warned on the draft check-your-answers page, committed as a system value at first submission and read back for the confirmation banner and dashboard Late tag, with competent-authority routing parked as backend work.
claims.quote: Every notifier-facing string says Great Britain and no address is checked by nation; the England-only drafting of the draft SI is parked as a legal note that changes no page. ... Lateness is computed in calendar days by one pure helper (potatoes late after arrivalDate minus 2, plants and wood late after arrivalDate plus 4, time ignored), shown live as a warning on the draft check-your-answers page, committed as a system value at the first submission (reconciled to D5's model) and read back for the banner on confirmation and the submitted view and the Late tag on the dashboard — all buildable now with no engine change — while routing to APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government is parked as backend work.

claims.statement: Docket D4-parties-and-contact (5 rulings) collapses the contact section to the single animals-shaped address-book pick because the picked record already carries name, address, telephone and email, deletes the plants-only number-and-email page and its two obligations, keeps Consignment Number as an optional notifier reference with its definition parked, asks the consignor only for plants for planting and wood, swaps 'the animal' for 'the consignment' in the country-of-origin error, and replaces the five animals declaration statements with three plants statements while parking the third-party authority clauses.
claims.quote: The contact section collapses to the single animals-shaped address-book pick: the picked record already carries the contact's name, address, telephone and email (the address book will not store a record without the last two), so the plants-only number-and-email page and its two obligations are deleted and Check your answers shows all four from the copied record. ... Nothing in this docket needs Sam.

claims.statement: Docket D2-commodity-model (15 rulings) stands the commodity model as drafted: one notification-level type (potatoes, plants for planting, wood and cut trees), nine per-line categories from the SI's scope items, one-or-many commodity lines, a fifteen-entry genus list served as reference data with hardwood narrowed to Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus, species as free text, seed potatoes treated as potatoes, every wood and potato scope condition carried as page guidance rather than a question, and a change of commodity type dropping incompatible lines in the commodity-type POST itself.
claims.quote: The commodity model stands as the reconciler drafted it: one notification-level type (potatoes, plants for planting, wood and cut trees), nine per-line categories taken straight from the SI's scope items, one-or-many commodity lines, a fifteen-entry genus list served as reference data with hardwood lines narrowed to Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus, species as free text, and seed potatoes treated as potatoes. ... Wipe wins over retain everywhere, and a change of commodity type after lines exist now drops the incompatible lines in the commodity-type POST itself (warning before, banner after), not on the list page's load, so stale lines can never reach the hub, check your answers or submission.

claims.statement: Docket D8-scope-and-parked (17 rulings) puts every item out of the first pass: the four conflicts resolve to the readings the spec already carries and all thirteen behaviours are parked rather than rejected, so nothing new is built — no agent or importer party, registration step, bulk upload, document import, regulator, inspector or analyst screens, list-maintenance admin, check booking, documents collection, outbox, event publishing or combined animals+plants list — with five small spec edits keeping the record honest.
claims.quote: Every item in this docket is out of the first pass and stays that way: the four conflicts resolve to the readings the spec already carries (proceed on the two Confluence pages as read; the signed-in Defra ID organisation is the notifier; Defra ID sign-in is the only precondition; many commodity lines in one notification is the commodityLines collection), and all thirteen behaviours are parked, not rejected.

claims.statement: Docket D3-origin-values-and-validation (11 rulings) settles what the origin page and the free-text fields may check: country of origin stays one field over the animals country list with the law's scope lists enforced on Continue (ware potatoes from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain; conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain; other plants and wood from an EU member state), Check your answers re-checks the rule, every unformatted field stays free text with a length cap, the only checks added are an arrival-time rule and a corrected quantity hint, the optional 'use' field is dropped, and the place of landing uses the built ports endpoint.
claims.quote: This docket settles what the origin page and the free-text fields may check. Country of origin stays one field over the animals country list (which already holds every country the law names), and the law's own scope lists are enforced when the notifier presses Continue: ware potatoes must come from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain, conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain, and other plants and wood from an EU member state
